_comment: M10 · MutationTier (harbor#44) — the tier table for paths under a Helm config dir.
WHAT A TIER MEANS. Not 'how bad would losing this be' — that is a backup
question. A tier answers 'what does writing here let an agent DO to the
floor'. Tier 0 disarms or forges. Tier 1 rewrites the thing that decides.
Tier 2 rewrites history. Tier 3 is ordinary session state.
guard_blocks AND deny ARE MEASURED, NOT INTENDED. Every value here was
recorded on 2026-08-05 by firing the real guard-selfedit.sh at the path in a
sandbox config dir, and by reading the complete permissions.deny array out of
settings.json with jq. Where the two layers disagree the table says so rather
than smoothing it over — the disagreements are the product of this ticket, and
SO A FALSE ENTRY HERE IS CAUGHT. tests/floor/mutation-tier-test.sh re-fires the guard
against every case and re-reads the deny array, so this file cannot quietly
drift from the surface it describes. That is the whole reason it is a fixture

tiers.0: teeth — integrity pins, the deny list itself, and the work-log credential. A write here disarms the floor or forges the record that would show it.
tiers.1: decider — the guard code, the hooks tree and the constitution. A write here changes what the floor decides, rather than switching it off.
tiers.2: record — the work-log and the guard-decision ledger. A write here rewrites history, not control.
tiers.3: ordinary — caches, transcripts, plugin and todo state. Session-writable by design; protecting it would be the false-positive class §2.11 is about.
